sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 both closed Monday at the top of their one-month range, up 2.8% and 5.3% respectively off their September lows. The VIX sits at 14.87, down nearly 17% from last month's high near 17.84, consistent with a low-volatility grind higher in US equities. Europe's Euro Stoxx 50 lags that move, sitting 2.6% off its own 1mo high and closer to the bottom of its range. Against that backdrop, 26 SP500/R1000/core operating names report this week, concentrated in industrials and technology, with Nike, Micron, Accenture, Procter & Gamble and Johnson & Johnson among the highest-profile prints.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Jefferies opens the week Monday reporting into the financial-services cluster, which has posted a mild +0.2% median 3-day reaction this cycle. United Airlines reports Tuesday into industrials, the week's largest sector present (627 tickers) and its most negative, running a -1.4% median. Micron reports Wednesday into technology, the best performer among sectors reporting this week at +0.9% median, while Nike closes out Thursday in the softer consumer-cyclical group (-0.2% median). KBR wraps the week Friday, also reporting into the industrials cluster.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the reaction table at +6.6% median across 176 tickers, on an unusually thick 2,630 news items. Alternative-asset-management (+2.9%, 6 tickers) and copper (+2.6%, 6 tickers) round out the top three, both on much lighter news volume (236 and 248 items). None of this week's SP500/R1000/core reporters sit inside these three sectors, so the strongest reaction signal this cycle isn't coming from the same names on deck to report.
